# 2021A Question 12 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Define**]{.task-verb} the terms “tolerance” and “tachyphylaxis” (30%). [**Discuss**]{.task-verb} the mechanisms by which these can develop, giving relevant examples (70%).
:::

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Define**]{.task-verb} both terms with their time courses for the first 30%, then [**discuss**]{.task-verb} mechanisms with named drug examples for the remaining 70%. Separate kinetic changes from receptor, signalling and physiological adaptations, and distinguish mediator depletion from other mechanisms.

::: {.structure-table}
| Feature | Tolerance | Tachyphylaxis |
|---|---|---|
| Definition and Time Course | | |
| Mediator or Pharmacokinetic Changes | | |
| Receptor and Signalling Adaptations | | |
| Other Physiological Adaptations | | |
| Drug Examples | | |
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**48.2%** of candidates achieved a pass in this question

The domains which attracted marks for this question were:

  - correct definition of both tachyphylaxis and tolerance
  - mechanisms for tachyphylaxis with examples
  - mechanisms for tolerance with examples

Common problems with the answers included:

  - not stating time course for these effects
  - confounding tolerance with ceiling effect/zero order kinetics/drug interactions
  - using phenylephrine as an example of an indirectly acting drug
  - confusing transmitter depletion with re-uptake inhibition
:::
